channel.title: RSS Aggregator Feed
channel.description: An aggregated feed of Technology-related news

item.title: India is starting to pay for apps, not just download them
item.description: India's app market generated a record $345 million in Q2.

item.title: Why are home servers trending? I took the plunge in an attempt to demystify the quiet tech community of tinkerers that are choosing to build, upcycle and host it themselves
item.description: More and more people are saving money and cutting down on e-waste by building home servers — and finding a ‘real sense of empowerment and independence’ along the way by being able to beat subscription fatigue.

item.title: SpaceXAI says it will take a year to fully remove unpermitted gas turbines from its Mississippi data center
item.description: The company was accused of violating the Clean Air Act by the NAACP.

item.title: What is a "tradwife"? Nara Smith rejects the viral label.
item.description: Nara Smith rejected the tradwife label on 'Call Her Daddy.' Here’s what the term means and why viewers still debate it.

item.title: Reminder: Dont use Google Maps for hiking
item.description: If you're planning a long hike, your phone map may not be your friend. Here's what you can use instead.

item.title: Regularly $599.99, this Samsung Odyssey OLED G6 monitor is $399.99 at Amazon if you act quickly
item.description: As of July 31, shop the Samsung 27-inch Odyssey OLED G6 gaming monitor for just $399.99 and save $200.

item.title: This hilarious robot collapse reminds me that robot development is nowhere near where it needs to be, but a huge breakthrough from DeepMind could change all that
item.description: Two recent robot demonstrations — one a huge fail and the other an inspiring breakthrough — remind us how far robots capable of living and working among us are from reality.

item.title: Google nixes its Earth AI feature one day after launch, amid criticism it would spread misinformation
item.description: A tool that allowed anyone to generate fake AI-generated imagery and superimpose it over real Google Earth maps quickly spurred backlash.

item.title: Amazon has $600 million in tariff refunds—and some of it is headed to customers
item.description: The retail giant says it will automatically return some tariff-related charges to eligible shoppers after collecting hundreds of millions in refunds. Amazon says that some customers will get back a sliver of cash from its pool of refunded money after the Trump administration’s tariffs experiment fell apart in court.

item.title: FIFA World Cup private investment plan explained: Why teams are vowing to boycott the controversial scheme
item.description: Team associations across Europe, Asia, and North America are pushing back hard against a plan they say treats the World Cup like an “investment product.” FIFA is not new to controversy: In the last decade, the international soccer association has faced bribery allegations, corruption scandals, and backlash over questionable host nation decisions.

item.title: Fresh off its Wiz payout, Index Ventures raises $2B across three funds
item.description: The new funding brings Index's total available investing capital to $3.5 billion.

item.title: Apple’s new AirTags are back down to their best price
item.description: We spotted a great deal on Tile trackers earlier this week that’s still live, but if you’re an iPhone owner, we ultimately recommend Apple’s latest AirTag. item.title: New York alleges Kalshi is running an 'illegal gambling operation' in new lawsuit
item.description: Kalshi, which is headquartered in New York, has already been sued by multiple states.

item.title: Google Earth’s AI deepfake tool only lasted one day
item.description: Google has shut down Google Earth feature it launched Thursday that allowed users to edit satellite images with text prompts using AI. The tool essentially let users create AI deepfakes of the real world using text prompts; Digital Digging's Henk van Ess, for example, intentionally generated images adding things like refugees near the Mexican border […]...

item.title: Snapchat is cracking down on AI slop in Spotlight
item.description: Videos made with AI will no longer appear in Snapchat's public recommendations.
